anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after two-click UI gating, draft-state arming, action routing, mux selection, local-event dispatch, route-layer continuation, asynchronous scheduling, request-material collection, input normalization, projection preparation and runtime transit recovery, whose own body constructs the target observable request signature token rather than merely collecting method/path/nonce/body/replay inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

primary_anchor.source_export: private closure returned by createSignatureReducer and selected through exported u(tuple, context); located in the bundle by fingerprint (the unique function referencing makeBody + makeTape + hasRequestSignatureEvidence and the 0x27d4eb2d mixing constant)
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible captures corpus only; grade by captured_span (byte offsets + sha256) plus answer_function. source_function is a private maintainer mapping and is not the agent answer space.
primary_anchor.why: Constructs the requested rs_ request_sig value from normalized request method, endpoint path, nonce window, body class, replay guard and recovered transit state.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Primary grading judgment: the submitted slice maps uniquely to one role_oracle captured_span by byte offsets and sha256 over the captures bundle; the matched row's score and role are awarded.
Secondary alignment: the submitted function_name equals the matched row's answer_function (the bundle slice's leading function name).
source_function is a private maintainer-only src/ mapping and never participates in grading the agent.
Agent identifies the captured-bundle function span corresponding to the primary anchor.

Agent explains why the answer constructs the request_sig value itself rather than collecting request inputs, handling either UI click, dispatching the local event, wrapping a payload, or logging the console object.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.
The answer must be constrained by both action vault.sign and field request_sig; rs-like decoy emitters are not sufficient.

role_oracle.why: Complete target-specific closure that derives the observable request_sig token from the normalized tuple, runtime transit state and active slot.
Checks that the tuple contains the request-specific evidence keys required for the real rs_ branch.
Serializes normalized tuple rows into reducer text before target-specific derivation.
Formats the mixed reducer state into the short body used by the rs_ value, but it is generic below the anchor.
Calls the selected reducer; it is a wrapper around the anchor rather than the constructor itself.
Handles the two-click UI gate and only releases the target envelope after the prepare click has armed a draft.
Stores the prepared request draft required before the release click can enter the target path.
Builds the publish-button envelope for the target action after verifying the prepared draft and replay guard.
Routes the vault.sign click envelope into the mux layer rather than directly into the event bridge.
Translates the publish button target into the vault.release mux branch before local event dispatch.
Moves the muxed release envelope through a DOM CustomEvent boundary before route continuation.
Collects request method, path, nonce, body class and replay guard material before projection.
Accesses alternate reducer slots for decoy paths and is not the target vault.sign request_sig constructor.

scoring_policy.primary_judgment: captured_span byte offsets + sha256 over the captures bundle
scoring_policy.source_level_answer: source_function is a private maintainer mapping and never grades the agent
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span equals the submitted span, or that uniquely contains / is uniquely contained by the submitted complete-function span; oversized spans covering multiple rows are ambiguous and score zero
scoring_policy.decoy_policy: rs-like values emitted outside action vault.sign and field request_sig score zero unless the submitted function is the primary anchor or an explicitly listed role.
scoring_policy.dynamic_path_summary: type #requestPath -> select #signatureMode prod -> select #requestMethod PATCH -> select #bodyClass ledger-close -> type #nonceInput -> check #entropyConsent -> click #prepareEnvelope -> click #publishSignature -> b1 clickPipeline -> b1 draft/envelope gate -> c2 action router -> d3 release mux -> g6 CustomEvent -> h7/i8/j9 -> f5 async scheduler -> e4 request material collector -> k1/k2/w* -> m0 projection and transit recovery -> requestSignatureTokenDerivation (selected via u) -> n0 console wrapper

oracle_notes: The visible page interaction is a two-click request-signature flow with no legacy form entrypoint.
The captured corpus remains a single obfuscated main-thread bundle with no source map.

The primary answer is the complete captured anchor closure (factory-returned requestSignatureTokenDerivation), not the enclosing createSignatureReducer factory unless the evaluator explicitly accepts enclosing-function expansion.

The click handler, draft builder, router, mux layer, CustomEvent bridge, async scheduler, request-material collector, projection caller and console sink are necessary path code but score below the anchor.
answer_function for module-level helpers is the readable source name (es output + renameGlobals:false); the anchor closure answer_function is the mangled bundle name discovered by gen_oracle_spans.
near_miss_not_accepted: prepare or publish click listener only
draft-state or replay-guard arming logic only
generic formatter or hash helper only
rs-like shadow_sig or preview_sig decoy emitter
